payload.rebuttal: fixed: Confirmed the finding by reading the code: with spec.touches == [] (a bug spec awaiting DIAGNOSE), `any(matches(path, pattern) for pattern in spec.touches)` is `any([])` = False, so `not any(...)` was True and retirement_refusal refused unconditionally for any marker naming that spec's id — permanently, since the refusal fires pre-cell in both build_queue and cli._run_cell, before DIAGNOSE (the only phase that could populate touches) is ever allowed to run. Fixed in saffron/scheduler.py by adding `_unmatched_criterion_path`'s own guard: the touches-unreached branch is now skipped when `spec.touches` is empty (`spec.touches and not any(...)`), so a bug spec's own marker no longer blocks it out of the queue. `forbidden` is deliberately NOT skipped alongside `touches`, since a bug spec can declare `forbidden` before DIAGNOSE runs and a file it may never touch is a permanent fact DIAGNOSE cannot change — refusing on that basis is still correct. Added three new tests: a unit test proving a bug spec with empty touches is not refused by its own marker, a unit test proving a bug spec's forbidden marker still refuses despite empty touches, and a build_queue-level integration test proving the bug spec is still admitted to the queue end to end despite carrying the marker. Committed as scheduler.py/tests/docs changes (commit adding the fix, tests, and docs/BACKLOG.md wording update); all 1024 tests pass and the diff remains under the `size` gate's feature ceiling (585/600 lines, measured with the gate's own `_changed_lines` function).
